cells.title: How do the post's statements about single sections compare with the records?
cells.takeaway: The records agree with the post at [[Canada|card:1223fa40#verdict/Canada]], [[Texas|card:1223fa40#verdict/Texas]], New York on May 17 and [[CDC|card:1223fa40#verdict/CDC]]. They differ on [[Justice's order of events|card:1223fa40#the%20records%20show/Justice]] and a [[budget portal count|card:1223fa40#the%20records%20show/MAX]], and cannot check the Census section or the [[BEA sign-up|card:1223fa40#verdict/BEA]].

import os, glob, json, pandas as pd
# "the post says" paraphrases https://transluce.org/us-canada-gov, section by section.

def cap(folder):
    d = pd.read_csv(f'{folder}/arquivo-captures.csv', dtype=str, keep_default_na=False)
    d['row'] = range(1, len(d) + 1)
    return d.sort_values(['captured_at_utc', 'row'])

def day(ts):
    t = pd.Timestamp(ts)
    return f'{t:%b} {t.day}'

rows = []

# Canada: the 13 payload requests listed in sources.csv and their stored texts
cs = pd.read_csv('02-canada/sources.csv', dtype=str, keep_default_na=False)
texts = [open('02-canada/' + f, encoding='utf-8').read().splitlines()[0] for f in cs.file if f]
nf = sum(t.strip() == 'Record not found.' for t in texts)
rows.append(('Canada', '13 payloads of 6 kinds, believed unsuccessful',
             f'{len(cs)} listed, all {"/".join(sorted(cs.http_status.unique()))}; {nf} of {len(texts)} texts "Record not found."',
             'agrees'))

# Texas: direct PDF exports of the STI data table
tr = pd.read_csv('07-texas/urlquery-reports.csv', dtype=str, keep_default_na=False)
th = pd.read_csv('07-texas/urlquery-http.csv', dtype=str, keep_default_na=False)
pdf = tr[tr.submitted_url.str.contains('DataTableBuilder.pdf')].report_id
signin = sum(bool(((th.report_id == r) & th.url.str.contains('auth/signin')).any()) for r in pdf)
rows.append(('Texas', 'could not confirm data came back',
             f'{len(pdf)} PDF exports, {signin} sent to sign-in; {int(th.response_mime.str.contains("pdf").sum())} PDFs',
             'agrees'))

# New York: on May 17, blocked first, then worked
ny = cap('06-new-york')
d17 = ny[ny.captured_at_utc.str.startswith('2026-05-17')]
d16 = ny[ny.captured_at_utc.str.startswith('2026-05-16')]
both = ny.groupby('target_url').indexed_http_status.agg(lambda s: {'200', '403'} <= set(s)).sum()
rows.append(('New York', 'May 17: first blocked, later worked',
             f'May 17: {d17.indexed_http_status.iloc[0]} then {d17.indexed_http_status.iloc[1]}; '
             f'May 16: {len(d16)} all {"/".join(d16.indexed_http_status.unique())}; {both} URLs got both',
             'agrees for May 17'))

# Justice: the encoded parent-folder trick and the redirects
j = cap('11-justice')
trick = j[j.target_url.str.contains(r'\.\.%2[Ff]', regex=True)]
redirect = j[j.indexed_http_status == '302'].iloc[0]
rows.append(('Justice', 'May 30-31: "..%2F" got past redirects',
             f'"..%2F" first {day(trick.captured_at_utc.iloc[0])} ({trick.indexed_http_status.iloc[0]}); '
             f'first redirect {day(redirect.captured_at_utc)}',
             'order differs'))

# MAX budget portal: distinct method/URL pairs in the urlquery scans
mh = pd.read_csv('09-max-gov/urlquery-http.csv', dtype=str, keep_default_na=False)
pairs = mh[['method', 'url']].drop_duplicates().shape[0]
rows.append(('MAX', '416 distinct method/URL pairs', f'{pairs} pairs', 'differs'))

# BEA: an attempted sign-up as "OpenAI Research", and a failed CAPTCHA reading
bea = pd.read_csv('12-bea/arquivo-captures.csv', dtype=str, keep_default_na=False)
signup = int(bea.target_url.str.contains(r'regist|sign-?up', case=False).sum())
files = [f for f in glob.glob('**/*', recursive=True) if f.endswith(('.csv', '.txt', '.json'))]
oair = sum('openai research' in open(f, encoding='utf-8', errors='replace').read().lower() for f in files)
bs = pd.read_csv('12-bea/sources.csv', dtype=str, keep_default_na=False)
withheld = int(bs.source_url.str.startswith('[WITHHELD').sum())
fn = json.load(open('12-bea/responses/35dbde93d88a7753.txt'))['data']['function']['value']
ocr = json.loads(json.loads(fn)['ocr'])['ParsedResults'][0]['ParsedText']
rows.append(('BEA', 'tried to register as "OpenAI Research"; CAPTCHA reading failed',
             f'{signup} sign-up URLs, {oair} files name it; {withheld} of {len(bs)} programs withheld; '
             f'OCR text {"empty" if ocr == "" else "found"}',
             'sign-up not checkable'))

# Census and CDC: evidence the post says it withheld
rows.append(('Census', 'URLs withheld', f'folder empty ({len(os.listdir("13-census"))} files)', 'withheld'))
cdc = pd.read_csv('15-cdc/sources.csv', dtype=str, keep_default_na=False)
body = open('15-cdc/' + cdc.file.iloc[0], encoding='utf-8').read().splitlines()
rows.append(('CDC', 'query-validation error; program link withheld',
             f'{len(cdc)} capture, {cdc.http_status.iloc[0]} "{body[1]}"', 'agrees'))

pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=['section', 'the post says', 'the records show', 'verdict']).set_index('section')

assessment.problem: The takeaway says the records agree with the post at New York, but the table only agrees for May 17: on May 16 all 12 captures got 200, and 5 URLs got both 200 and 403.
